justification: Fixes a silent wrong-eligibility bug in the shared Housing-SEPP engine: in_lmr_area was derived as 'not on the 776 exclusion map', which over-includes all of regional NSW because 776 only carves out spots INSIDE covered areas — absence from the exclusion map is not inclusion. Proven live 2026-07-13/14: 38 Park Rd Bowral (no town centre, TOD or exclusion feature within 1 km) was reported in the reform area by the engine while Verify's LGA check and the SEPP's s22 definition say it is not. The engine feeds BOTH the live public upzoning tool and the intelligence brief, so the false in-area answer could surface eligible LMR forms (terraces green) in towns the reform does not cover. New derivation: anchored (within 800 m of a Town Centres Map (766) polygon OR inside a TOD catchment 752/759) AND NOT excluded (776), fail-closed on every query.

pre_impl.existing_data: Everything reused, nothing re-implemented: query_arcgis_point_buffered already existed in portal_constraints with a distance_m parameter (built for buffered layer queries); fetch_tod_catchment and fetch_sepp_exclusions already produce the other two terms of the new derivation; the EPLANNING_LAYERS registry pattern was extended with one entry (766). The LMR prescope plan (ce-lmr-pipeline-prescope-2026-06) had already mapped the derivation approach and flagged the 776-semantics risk that this fix resolves.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The shipped engine assumed absence from the 776 exclusion map means the reform applies — the optimistic reading of an ambiguity the prescope plan explicitly flagged as unresolved risk two. Live enumeration re-confirmed 2026-07-14 that no inclusion layer exists (only 752/759/766/776), and the live Bowral probe showed zero anchor features within a kilometre of a lot the old gate reported as in-area, falsifying the assumption.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: one fetcher (fetch_town_centre_catchment, a thin buffered query over layer 766) and the boolean composition inside _gate_inputs. Explicitly NOT built: no new PostGIS ingestion (live ArcGIS query per the prescope architecture decision), no walking-network computation (radial 800 m proxy, documented as slightly generous at the margin), and no change to Verify's separate frontend isLMRApplicable check (consolidation to this gate is the eligibility-consolidation plan's scope, not this PR).
pre_impl.external_source_error: Every external call is fail-closed: a 766 query failure leaves near_town_centre False (test-pinned), a 776 failure leaves not_excluded False, a TOD failure leaves in_tod False — any failure path yields in_lmr_area False, so an outage can only under-report eligibility, never grant it. The buffered query uses the shared 8-second ArcGIS timeout and the public no-key endpoint that the existing gates already depend on.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend type changes: the gates dict keeps the identical shape ({in_lmr_area, in_tod, dual_occ_prohibited}, all booleans), so the upzoning page chips and the brief's eligibility card consume it unchanged; only the truth value for unanchored regional lots flips from True to False, which the existing 'Not in a Low and Mid-Rise reform area (or area unconfirmed)' engine wording already covers.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a regional homeowner could see terraces or apartments rendered as meeting reform standards in a town the reform does not cover — a silent false positive on a public page and in the brief. After: unanchored lots read 'Not in a Low and Mid-Rise reform area'; the residual failure mode is the conservative direction (a lot between the 766 radial buffer and true walking distance may read out-of-area, and station-precinct anchors outside published TOD polygons are not yet derived), which under-reports and is documented in the code comment.

functions.name: fetch_town_centre_catchment
functions.input: Latitude and longitude in GDA94 plus an optional buffer distance in metres defaulting to 800
functions.output: Dict with within_catchment boolean and the matched town centre LABEL string, or None when the ArcGIS query fails entirely
functions.if_none: Callers must treat None as not anchored — _gate_inputs wraps the call in try/except and leaves near_town_centre False on None or exception, so a layer outage can never place a lot inside the reform area

functions.name: _gate_inputs
functions.input: Optional latitude and longitude of the resolved lot centroid
functions.output: Dict of the three gate booleans: in_lmr_area (now anchored AND not excluded), in_tod, dual_occ_prohibited
functions.if_none: Missing coordinates return all-False immediately; each gate query failure logs a warning and leaves its term at the conservative False, so partial outages degrade to fewer eligible forms rather than wrong eligible forms

values.if_missing: Stays False on None or exception — the anchor term simply does not fire and in_lmr_area falls back to the TOD anchor or False
Stays False on None or exception, which zeroes in_lmr_area regardless of anchors — an exclusion-map outage can never un-exclude a lot
Stays False; the lot loses the TOD anchor and mid-rise forms show the engine's not-in-catchment wording

queries: N/A - no SQL changes. All three touched paths are live ArcGIS point/buffer queries against public NSW ePlanning layers; the only DB read in the engine (housing_sepp_standards) is untouched.

break_it.scenario: Regional lot far from any nominated centre reported inside the reform area because it is absent from the sparse 776 exclusion map (the exact Bowral production bug this PR fixes)
break_it.what_happens: Terraces and apartment forms render as meeting reform standards on the public tool and in the brief for towns the reform does not cover — a silent false positive in eligibility
break_it.how: in_lmr_area now requires a positive anchor (766 within 800 m or inside TOD) AND not-excluded; test_gate_inputs_not_excluded_alone_is_NOT_in_lmr_area pins it and the live Bowral re-run shows all LMR forms reading not-in-area
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py::test_gate_inputs_not_excluded_alone_is_NOT_in_lmr_area; live run of 38 Park Rd Bowral recorded in the PR

break_it.scenario: Town Centres layer query dies mid-request and the lot silently gains the anchor anyway
break_it.what_happens: A network flake would convert into reform-area membership and potentially green LMR forms
break_it.how: the fetcher returns None on failure and _gate_inputs leaves near_town_centre False on None or exception; test_gate_inputs_town_centre_query_failure_is_not_falsely_anchored pins the fail-closed direction

break_it.scenario: A genuinely anchored lot inside a nominated catchment loses eligibility because the new AND-composition is wired backwards
break_it.what_happens: Under-reporting in the covered areas — the tool stops showing reform rights where they genuinely exist, a correctness regression in the other direction
break_it.how: positive-path tests pin both anchors independently (town-centre-only and TOD-only both yield in_lmr_area True when not excluded), and the live Gladesville town-centre centroid probe plus the live Kogarah TOD lot both return True post-change

break_it.scenario: A lot inside a 776 exclusion carve-out but near a town centre reads as in-area because exclusion is no longer consulted
break_it.what_happens: The exclusion map exists precisely to remove such lots from the reform — ignoring it would over-report in the carved-out pockets
break_it.how: the composition is anchored AND not_excluded; test_gate_inputs_anchored_but_excluded_is_not_in_lmr_area pins that an excluded lot stays out even with both anchors true

break_it.scenario: The radial 800 m buffer over-includes lots that are within 800 m straight-line but beyond 800 m walking distance of a centre (s22 says walking distance)
break_it.what_happens: A margin of lots just outside true walking range could read in-area — over-report at the boundary, the direction the doctrine forbids
break_it.how: accepted, documented proxy: the fetcher docstring and gate comment state radial superset-of walking; the per-form standards still gate downstream, consent wording remains subject-to-DA, and the ineligible wording already hedges with area-unconfirmed phrasing; a walking-network refinement is out of scope and recorded in the code comment
break_it.repro: read services/portal_constraints.py fetch_town_centre_catchment docstring — the proxy and its direction are stated in the shipped code

break_it.scenario: Station-precinct anchors that sit outside published TOD polygons are not derived (station point data is not ingested), so some legitimately covered lots read out-of-area
break_it.what_happens: Under-reporting near stations that lack a published TOD polygon — conservative but incomplete coverage of the s22 definition
break_it.how: accepted conservative gap, inherited from the prescope plan's phase-three scope: under-report is the doctrine-permitted direction; deriving station-point catchments is the documented follow-up and cannot produce false positives meanwhile
break_it.repro: ce-lmr-pipeline-prescope-2026-06 phase 3 records the station-data dependency; the gate comment references the derivation basis

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after Railway deploy, re-run 38 Park Rd Bowral on the live tool (LMR chip must read not-established and terraces must read not-in-area) and 67 Warialda St Kogarah (must stay fully eligible); spot-check one town-centre-anchored Sydney address renders LMR forms. The brief inherits the gate silently - regenerate any cached Bowral-area briefs if surfaced to users.
